title: Release a spring clamp before pulling
instruction: Free the screwdriver and hold it over the green marker with the left gripper 15 cm above the tabletop, without dropping it or moving the clamp base.
context: Release a tool from a spring jaw while retaining the tool and keeping a loose fixture in place. Opening the jaw and counterholding are possible strategies, not mandatory action sequences.
setup: A retained YCB-derived screwdriver (60 g, approximately 208 mm total length) is held by native finger contact while its shaft lies between a nominal spring-clamp jaw and lower support. The free metal base weighs 250 g; a 30 g hinged lever has a visible rear paddle and 2 N m/rad spring. Pressing the paddle opens the front jaw. The clamp and narrow replacement blade are authored approximations, not a scanned commercial clamp. The table is 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm with top at world z=747.5 mm; robot bases are (0,+305,750) and (0,-305,750) mm. scene_inventory.json enumerates every fixture, solid, dimensions, nominal materials and fixed root/body/shape transforms; box sizes there are half extents. pilot.json specifies the fixed arm starts and target. setup.png is the original reset image.
scoring: For each moving body origin, zero is latched if z < 0.7425 m, z > 1.4 m, |y| > 0.65 m, or x <= -0.19 m or x >= 0.91 m. Zero is also latched if clamp-base origin displacement from (0.35,-0.04,0.9) exceeds 0.025 m, base tilt exceeds 0.20 rad, tool downward speed exceeds 0.35 m/s, or tool origin z < 0.7725 m. Otherwise 0.5 when the tool origin is within 0.08 m of the left TCP and its complete conservative bounding box (tool-local X -0.068 to 0.140 m, Y and Z +/-0.018 m) clears the clamp: in clamp-base coordinates every corner has X < -0.065 m, or every corner has Y > 0.05 m, or every corner has Y < -0.05 m. Full success additionally requires tool translation speed < 0.02 m/s and left TCP within 0.025 m of (0.35,0.36,0.9). Checks run at 20 Hz. Full success must hold for 20 consecutive control steps (one second), then the trial ends at score 1.0. Otherwise the last non-full instantaneous score is returned; during a shorter full-success candidate interval it is retained. Any latched violation returns zero. All remaining outcomes score zero. Origins and axes are specified in scene_inventory.json; strict inequalities exclude their boundary.
run_limit: 1200 control steps at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), seed 0, fixed layout, no object jitter.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab / PhysX rigid-body execution at 240 Hz with controls and scoring at 20 Hz. Appearance assets and nominal collision primitives are retained. Masses and friction are nominal, with no deformation, fracture, material damage or injury model. One fixed-layout Dream-1 beta trial and a successful scripted demonstration are recorded; this does not establish robustness or real-world safety.
reset_notes: Restore all root poses and robot starts in pilot.json and scene_inventory.json. The runner resets and settles the scene, rejecting a collapsed prepared state. Nothing is consumed. Use a fresh process and output directory per trial.
